Marvila — Lisbon, Portugal

🟡 Local press research

Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Marvila is the most heavily and repeatedly documented of the five for serious drug-related crime, largely centred on the Chelas public-housing area within it. Visão (3 Oct 2024) reported the conviction, to 19 years, of "Samir, rei do crack," leader of the so-called "grupo de Chelas"; Observador's special report described how PSP dismantled a group "controlled by terror" running one of Lisbon's busiest open-air drug points, earning about €3,000/day. Correio da Manhã separately reported Chelas youths threatening rivals with gun photos online, and JN reported an 11kg drug network dismantled in Chelas. PSP operations recur into 2025-2026: CNN Portugal covered a Marvila weapons/drugs cordon (Dec 2023), TVI/CNN reported four detained with drugs and guns seized in a Marvila bairro operation (21 Jan 2026), and TVI reported joint PSP searches of 12 homes across Olivais and Marvila (17 Dec 2025). Sources checked: Visão, 3 Oct 2024 – "Samir, rei do crack, líder do 'grupo de Chelas', foi condenado a 19 anos de prisão"; Observador (special) – "Grupo controlado pelo 'terror' e que rendia 3 mil euros por dia"; Correio da Manhã – "Grupo de jovens de Chelas ameaçam rivais de droga com fotografias de armas na 'net'"; Jornal de Notícias – "Policia desmantela rede de tráfico na zona de Chelas e apreende 11 quilos de droga"; CNN Portugal, 12 Dec 2023 – "Operação da PSP cerca Marvila à procura de armas e droga"; TVI Notícias / CNN Portugal, 21 Jan 2026 – "Quatro detidos, droga e armas apreendidas em operação da PSP em bairro de Lisboa" (Marvila); TVI Notícias, 17 Dec 2025 – "PSP faz buscas em 12 casas nos Olivais e em Marvila".
